purpose: Live Power Stack thematic radar. Rankings are rebuilt each run from freshness/materiality and current market significance; stale themes are demoted rather than archived near the top. Theme rank changes research priority and proof requirements, not company fundamental scores.

environment.label: $100 oil + duration resistance + record physical power demand
environment.summary: Refined-product and shipping inflation are colliding with a long-end bond market that resisted Treasury liquidity support, while AI/data-centre physical demand remains record-strong but increasingly debt-intensive. Equity breadth is weakening, yet earnings revisions remain constructive, producing extreme dispersion rather than a clean broad risk-off regime.

whatIsNewNow: U.S. refining is operating with little slack: EIA shows about 18.0m b/d operable capacity and 98% utilization in late August; the useful signal is tight spare capacity plus high cracks/distillate stress, not the creator claim that capacity is the lowest ever.
Treasury scheduled up to $6bn of 10-20Y buybacks for Sep 10, yet the 10Y reached about 4.85% after the announcement: a useful duration-clearing/news-failure signal ahead of PPI/CPI.

AI financing is now a first-class macro variable: hyperscaler debt issuance has accelerated sharply while ECB/credit-market evidence shows potential crowding-out and tighter underwriting around AI infrastructure.
U.S. power demand remains record-strong from data centres/manufacturing, while Europe/Asia LNG competition is intensifying as Gulf flows are disrupted.
Equity breadth and small caps are weakening under higher rates, but positive S&P earnings revisions argue for a fragility/concentration overlay rather than a standalone crash thesis.
whatMattersMostToMarketsNow: Long-end/real-yield clearing rates and weak-end credit

promoteWhen: Fresh evidence materially changes transmission, breadth or investability
At least two independent evidence streams converge
parkWhen: No material fresh evidence and low current cross-asset transmission
Narrative lacks commercial, physical or balance-sheet confirmation
A broader theme subsumes the mechanism

themes.name: Middle East Refined Products + Shipping Stress
themes.whyNow: Brent is above $100 while renewed Hormuz shipping attacks collide with tight distillate conditions. EIA shows roughly 18.0m b/d of U.S. operable refining capacity and 98% utilization in late August: the important constraint is little spare refining slack plus high cracks, not an all-history capacity low.
themes.marketTransmission: Diesel/jet inflation, refining margins, tanker rates, insurance, freight, farmer inputs, consumer purchasing power and bond yields.
themes.confirmation: Hormuz traffic remains depressed, refinery utilization/cracks stay elevated, product inventories stay tight and war-risk costs persist.
themes.invalidation: Durable de-escalation plus normalized flows and sustained collapse in product cracks/insurance/freight.
themes.nextTest: EIA weekly products/utilization, Hormuz vessel counts/insurance and Sep 10 PPI/Sep 11 CPI transmission.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: HOLD XOM/HIBISCS/MISC with discipline; favor integrated/refining/logistics over chasing pure crude beta.
watch: Check U.S. refinery utilization, ULSD/jet cracks and distillate inventories rather than repeating the 'lowest capacity ever' claim.
Check whether Hormuz vessel counts, insurance and freight confirm persistent physical disruption.

mainNews.title: Elevated crack spreads and crude oil prices contribute to higher prices at the pump
mainNews.implication: Refining/product tightness is transmitting the crude shock into consumer and freight inflation.

themes.name: Global Duration / Real-Yield + Weak-End Credit Stress
themes.whyNow: Treasury scheduled up to $6bn of 10-20Y buybacks for Sep 10 after previously increasing long-end liquidity support, yet the 10Y still reached about 4.85% after the announcement as $100 oil reinforced inflation risk. The response is a clearing-rate/news-failure signal, not proof that buybacks are universally ineffective.
themes.marketTransmission: Higher hurdle rates, tighter project underwriting, lower equity-duration tolerance, housing pressure, weak-end credit stress and dispersion toward cash-generative businesses.
themes.confirmation: Long yields remain elevated through PPI/CPI, weak-end credit stays stressed and rate-sensitive breadth/small caps continue to lag.
themes.invalidation: Sustained long-yield compression plus improving credit and breadth without renewed inflation.
themes.nextTest: Sep 10 Treasury buyback/yield reaction and PPI, Sep 11 CPI, Sep 15-16 FOMC and Sep 17-18 BOJ.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Raise proof/valuation hurdle for TTWO/TSLA and financing-heavy AI/nuclear; prioritize FCF/backlog quality.
watch: Check whether the Sep 10 buyback actually changes the 10Y/30Y clearing rate, auction tone or real yields.
Use breadth as a fragility overlay: RSP/SPY, percent above 50D, advance-decline and Russell 2000 versus yields.

mainNews.title: US Treasury to buy up to $6 billion in Sept 10 buyback operation
mainNews.implication: Long-end support was increased while yields still rose, strengthening the duration-clearing-rate question.

mainNews.title: Stocks pare some losses, but breadth stays firmly negative
mainNews.implication: Weak participation and small-cap sensitivity make high yields more dangerous even while headline indices remain near highs.

themes.name: Power / Grid / Cooling + Record Electricity Demand
themes.whyNow: EIA forecasts record U.S. electricity sales of 4,135 BkWh in 2026 and 4,211 BkWh in 2027, explicitly driven by data-centre development and manufacturing. Google's new Finland AI-infrastructure commitment plus long-dated nuclear power purchase reinforces that physical demand remains real even as financing costs rise.
themes.marketTransmission: Generation, transmission, substations, switchgear, transformers, cooling, gas/nuclear generation and utility capex.
themes.confirmation: Energised MW, signed PPAs, firm load, real equipment orders/backlog and strong cash conversion.
themes.invalidation: Broad cancellation of funded projects or sustained weakening in orders/utilisation despite proposed load.
themes.nextTest: Supplier backlog/orders, utility interconnection awards, signed PPAs and regional power-demand updates.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Maintain PWR/ETN/GEV/VRT priority; YTLPOWR thesis strong but add only on funded utilisation/FCF proof.
watch: Separate requested/interconnection-queue MW from funded, permitted and energised MW.
Check electrical-equipment backlog, power contracts and cash conversion as financing costs rise.

mainNews.title: EIA expects record electricity generation in 2026 and 2027
mainNews.implication: Official demand forecasts independently confirm the data-centre/manufacturing power-load theme.

themes.name: AI Financing Quality + Cash Conversion
themes.whyNow: AI/data-centre demand remains strong, but financing has become a macro constraint. Hyperscaler bond issuance has accelerated sharply in 2026, ECB analysis flags potential crowding-out in euro corporate debt, and project lenders are tightening terms around permits, leases, guarantees and completion risk.
themes.marketTransmission: Project hurdle rates, dilution, credit spreads, customer concentration, debt-market crowding and equity FCF conversion.
themes.confirmation: Signed leases/PPAs, deposits, customer guarantees, manageable new-issue concessions and improving FCF.
themes.invalidation: Funding stress/cancellations spread into high-quality backlog and actual demand weakens.
themes.nextTest: AI IG/CDS spreads, new-issue concessions, capital raises, project covenants and supplier cash-conversion updates.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Prefer funded picks-and-shovels and strong balance sheets; high capex without cash conversion requires a higher hurdle.
watch: Track AI/hyperscaler bond issuance, spreads, new-issue concessions and structured/project-debt terms.
Check whether capex growth is translating into signed demand, operating cash flow and free cash flow rather than just capacity announcements.

mainNews.title: Big tech, big debt: when US tech giants tap the euro area bond market
mainNews.implication: AI financing demand is large enough to affect corporate-bond supply, pricing and crowding-out risk.

themes.name: Energy Security Rerouting + US LNG / Alternative Corridors
themes.whyNow: U.S. LNG exports averaged about 17.4 Bcf/d in H1 2026, up 23% y/y, while Gulf disruption has tightened European gas and reduced Middle East LNG availability. Europe enters the next heating season with much lower storage than a year ago, increasing competition for Atlantic cargoes and the strategic value of U.S. LNG, storage and alternative corridors.
themes.marketTransmission: TTF/JKM and electricity inflation, US LNG contracts, tankers, storage/terminals, pipelines, industrial margins and central-bank easing room.
themes.confirmation: High U.S. LNG utilization/feedgas, persistent Europe/Asia cargo competition, long-term contracts and sustained rerouting/tonne-miles.
themes.invalidation: Rapid Gulf normalization, strong storage recovery and no persistent diversification spending/contracts.
themes.nextTest: U.S. LNG feedgas/exports, TTF/JKM, EU storage, Gulf loadings, contract announcements and bypass traffic.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: LNG remains a preferred strategic exposure; avoid treating spot-gas convexity as permanent.
watch: Track Europe storage and TTF/JKM together with Qatari/Middle East LNG loadings.
Check U.S. LNG feedgas/utilization and long-term contract activity rather than spot price alone.

mainNews.title: Europe's winter gas drama could leave deep scars
mainNews.implication: Lower storage and disrupted Gulf LNG raise Atlantic-basin competition and electricity/industrial inflation risk.

themes.name: Copper: Grid Scarcity vs China Divergence
themes.whyNow: Copper remains near record levels around $14.7k/t as mine/supply scarcity and grid/AI electrification demand persist. At the same time, weak Chinese private-demand indicators argue against treating the move as proof of broad China reflation.
themes.marketTransmission: Producer cash flow versus higher input costs for electrical equipment, cables, construction and irrigation.
themes.confirmation: Ex-US inventory draw, physical premiums, mine constraints and grid/electrical orders remain firm.
themes.invalidation: Visible inventory rebuild plus weaker grid/industrial orders and physical premiums.
themes.nextTest: LME/SHFE inventories, China premiums, mine disruptions and utility/electrical order data.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: FCX thesis confirmed but do not chase; first useful retest ~72-74, stronger ~68-70.
watch: Require physical inventories/premiums and grid orders to confirm record copper rather than relying on price alone.
Keep China private credit/property demand separate from state/grid/AI copper demand.

mainNews.title: Anglo-Teck wait shows mining M&A's rising toll
mainNews.implication: Record copper and scarce high-quality assets reinforce the supply-scarcity side of the thesis.

themes.name: Gold / Silver: Reserve Diversification vs Real Yields
themes.whyNow: Official-sector and ETF flows are reinforcing gold despite elevated nominal/real yields. World Gold Council data show China bought 20t and Poland 8t in July, while August global gold ETFs added about $18bn and 121t to record holdings. The transcript's China '20t in August' label is not propagated because the independently verified 20t purchase was July.
themes.marketTransmission: Physical bullion, quality miners, reserve diversification and fiscal/geopolitical hedging; tactical timing remains vulnerable to a real-yield/USD breakout.
themes.confirmation: Bullion holds/rises through hot inflation and high real yields, official/ETF flows persist, or real yields roll over.
themes.invalidation: Persistent real-yield/USD breakout with bullion losing major trend support and flows reversing.
themes.nextTest: PPI/CPI, real10Y/DXY, central-bank reserve updates and ETF flows.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Strategic exposure valid; stage entries rather than chase.
watch: Verify central-bank purchase month/tonnage from WGC or official reserve data before using creator claims.
Track ETF flows together with real yields and DXY to separate structural reserve demand from tactical price momentum.

mainNews.title: Gold ETF Flows: August 2026
mainNews.implication: Large August ETF inflows add a market-flow confirmation layer to official-sector reserve diversification.

themes.name: Agriculture Weather + Black Sea Trade Rerouting
themes.whyNow: Argentina's Aug-Sep corn exports are set for a record 10m tonnes as Ukrainian/European supply routes tighten, while super-El Nino heat/drought has driven exceptional Indonesian wildfire emissions and hotspots. Energy/freight inflation raises the affordability risk even if crop prices rise.
themes.marketTransmission: Grain prices, food CPI, farm margins, seed/fertilizer demand, freight and emerging-market inflation/policy.
themes.confirmation: Persistent Black Sea disruption, crop/weather downgrades and rising crop prices relative to farm inputs.
themes.invalidation: Weather normalizes without meaningful crop damage and trade routes/prices normalize.
themes.nextTest: USDA/crop estimates, El Nino progression, palm/grain output and crop/input price ratios.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CTVA/BG preferred over machinery until farm economics improve; AGCO remains second-stage cyclical watch.

themes.name: Fertilizer / Nitrogen Scarcity vs Farm Affordability
themes.whyNow: Energy/shipping disruption supports nitrogen economics while diesel and input inflation squeeze farmer margins. Weather/trade-route food inflation increases crop-price support but does not make farm-input demand fully inelastic.
themes.marketTransmission: Nitrogen/feedstock pricing, farmer margins and demand elasticity across fertilizer/seed/crop protection/machinery.
themes.confirmation: Healthy crop/input ratios, firm urea/ammonia and stable application rates.
themes.invalidation: Farmer margins deteriorate enough to cause broad input deferral despite high fertilizer prices.
themes.nextTest: Urea/ammonia/gas, crop prices, application rates and company guidance.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CF quality thesis strong but entry crowded; CTVA preferred as less-deferable genetics exposure.

themes.name: Uranium / Nuclear Fuel-Cycle Scarcity
themes.whyNow: Energy security and power demand keep nuclear structurally relevant, but there is no equally material fresh commercial contracting evidence today. North Korea enrichment developments are geopolitical security evidence, not direct commercial uranium demand.
themes.marketTransmission: Fuel/conversion/enrichment contracting, proven nuclear components and power-security capex.
themes.confirmation: Long-term contracting, conversion/enrichment scarcity and funded reactor/component awards.
themes.invalidation: Supply materially outruns utility contracting or funded-project economics deteriorate.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: CCJ/BWXT/CW remain preferred over pre-revenue reactor duration; CCJ ideal closer to $95-100.

themes.name: Selective AI Software / Cybersecurity + Physical Operations Software
themes.whyNow: AI demand remains strong in selected vendors, but high real yields reject blanket SaaS expansion. Mission-critical cyber and software tied to measurable physical operations/ARR/FCF remain preferable.
themes.marketTransmission: ARR/RPO/FCF, security spend, operational productivity and duration multiples.
themes.confirmation: Durable AI-linked growth with expanding margins/FCF across multiple vendors.
themes.invalidation: Growth slows while multiples stay elevated or AI monetization fails to translate to cash.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Use pullbacks; CRWD near ~$208 is worth selective research, not blanket SaaS buying.

themes.name: AI Inference + Optical Connectivity Diversification
themes.whyNow: Qualcomm and Amazon announced a multi-generation collaboration for customized AI inference silicon plus optical connectivity up to 1.6T; potential Amazon purchases and warrants make execution, margin and dilution proof more important than headline TAM.
themes.marketTransmission: Inference silicon, power-efficient compute, optical connectivity, industrial/robotics AI and hyperscaler capex diversification.
themes.confirmation: Material data-centre revenue ramp, additional hyperscaler wins, attractive margins/FCF and manageable dilution.
themes.invalidation: Handset decline overwhelms diversification, data-centre ramp slips, economics require excessive concessions or valuation outruns execution.
themes.nextTest: QCOM valuation/FCF profile, customer concentration, product ramp and next earnings guidance.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: NEW PRIORITY RESEARCH / DO NOT CHASE; no entry zone until underwriting is complete.

themes.name: ESS Demand vs Battery Manufacturing Overcapacity
themes.whyNow: Grid/peak-load economics support storage deployment while China is screening new storage-battery capacity because manufacturing supply is excessive.
themes.marketTransmission: Benefits integrators/VPP/grid deployment more than undifferentiated cell/lithium capacity.
themes.confirmation: Storage deployments/FCF grow while cell-capacity rationalization improves industry economics.
themes.invalidation: Storage deployment slows materially or commodity overcapacity overwhelms integrator margins.
themes.nextTest: ESS deployments, capacity closures/consolidation and battery pricing.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: TSLA storage remains best current earnings bridge; SGML stays speculative/no promotion.

themes.name: Selective Automation Before Humanoids
themes.whyNow: No fresh evidence changes the commercialization order. Established warehouse/factory automation still has clearer ROI and deployment proof than humanoids.
themes.marketTransmission: Warehouse/factory capex, labor substitution, machine vision, motion control and industrial productivity.
themes.confirmation: Real deployments, order growth, improving margins and customer ROI.
themes.invalidation: Broad established-automation slowdown while humanoids demonstrate superior commercial economics at scale.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Hierarchy remains fixed/warehouse -> cobots/mobile -> industrial humanoids -> general-purpose.

themes.name: China Weak Private-Credit Transmission + State Balance Sheets
themes.whyNow: No fresh credit release today changes the prior weak private/household transmission read. State infrastructure remains the more reliable China channel.
themes.marketTransmission: Favours state-backed power/infrastructure and verified exporters over broad consumer/property reflation beta.
themes.confirmation: State capex/orders remain strong while household/property credit stays weak.
themes.invalidation: Sustained rebound in household/private credit, property and retail demand.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Do not use record copper alone as proof of broad China reflation.

themes.name: Consumer Credit / Trade-Down Bifurcation
themes.whyNow: Oil above $100 plus food/fuel inflation and high financing costs reduce real discretionary flexibility, but there is no evidence of a broad collapse.
themes.marketTransmission: Travel/discretionary/housing pressure; trade-down and collateral-credit resilience.
themes.confirmation: Delinquencies/trade-down rise while real spending breadth weakens.
themes.invalidation: Real income improves and energy/financing costs fall materially.
themes.nextTest: Consumer credit, delinquencies and inflation data.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Background risk filter rather than standalone broad trade.

themes.name: Early Cyclical Recovery: Ag Equipment / Irrigation / Lumber
themes.whyNow: Higher crop prices and trade disruption are not enough to call a machinery/irrigation recovery while financing costs and farmer input burdens remain elevated.
themes.marketTransmission: Farm capex, machinery orders, irrigation replacement and construction/lumber demand.
themes.confirmation: Improving farm margins plus order/backlog inflection and easier financing.
themes.invalidation: Farm economics deteriorate further or equipment orders remain weak.
themes.nextTest: Farm income/crop-input ratios and machinery guidance.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: AGCO remains second-stage only; VMI is preferred because grid/water exposure diversifies the farm cycle.

themes.name: Generic Lithium Miner Reflation
themes.whyNow: Strong ESS demand has not repaired industry-wide manufacturing/miner oversupply and dilution economics. Isolated supply interruptions are insufficient.
themes.marketTransmission: Lithium prices, miner FCF/dilution and battery cost curves.
themes.confirmation: Sustained lithium price recovery with capacity rationalization and better producer FCF.
themes.invalidation: Continued oversupply, dilution and weak margins.
themes.nextTest: Capacity closures, lithium pricing and miner balance sheets.
themes.watchlistHoldingAction: Do not promote generic miners; prefer ESS deployment/integration.
